days.title: What is cybersecurity? + set up your learning system
tasks: Read 'Phase 0 - What is Cybersecurity?' in the roadmap
Create free accounts: TryHackMe, picoCTF, PortSwigger Academy
Create a GitHub repo called `cybersec-notes` - every day's notes go here
Pick a notes app (Obsidian or plain Markdown in that repo)
days.challenge: In 5 lines, write what cybersecurity protects and why. Include one real breach you read about on Krebs on Security.

days.title: Ethics, law & responsible disclosure
tasks: Read 'Ethical & Legal Boundaries' in the roadmap - twice
Read the OWASP Vulnerability Disclosure cheat sheet
Look up your country's computer-misuse law (e.g. IT Act 2000 s.43/66 in India, CFAA in the US)
days.challenge: Write your personal 'rules of engagement' (3 rules) and commit them as the first file in cybersec-notes.

days.title: Explore the domains (don't choose yet!)
tasks: Study the domain mindmap in the roadmap (Offensive, AppSec, Defensive, Investigative, ...)
Watch one NetworkChuck video about cybersecurity careers
Search LinkedIn for one job post each in 3 domains that sound interesting
days.challenge: For 3 domains, write one line each: 'A normal day in this job looks like ...'

days.title: Build a news habit + NIST Cybersecurity Framework
tasks: Read 3 articles on The Hacker News
Skim the NIST CSF 2.0 functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
Subscribe/bookmark: The Hacker News, Krebs on Security
days.challenge: Pick one incident from today's news and map what went wrong to the CSF functions.

days.title: Build your home lab: VirtualBox + Ubuntu VM
tasks: Install VirtualBox (or VMware Workstation Player)
Download Ubuntu Desktop LTS and install it as a VM (2 CPU, 4 GB RAM, 30 GB disk)
Install guest additions, update with `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade`
Do NOT install Kali yet - the roadmap explains why
days.challenge: Take a VM snapshot named `clean-install`. Screenshot it into your notes.

days.title: How a computer runs a program (CPU, RAM, storage)
tasks: Watch CS50x Lecture 0 (first hour is enough)
Learn: CPU, RAM vs storage, fetch-decode-execute cycle
days.challenge: In your VM, find: number of CPU cores, total RAM and disk size. Explain fetch-decode-execute in 3 sentences.

days.title: Week 1 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: What is cybersecurity? + set up your learning system; Ethics, law & responsible disclosure; Explore the domains (don't choose yet!); Build a news habit + NIST Cybersecurity Framework; Build your home lab: VirtualBox + Ubuntu VM; How a computer runs a program (CPU, RAM, storage)
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'What is cybersecurity? + set up your learning system' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Processes, memory & filesystems - what an OS does
tasks: Do the TryHackMe room 'Operating Systems Introduction'
Learn: process vs program, PID, virtual memory, filesystem
days.challenge: Using `top`, find the process using the most memory in your VM. What is its PID and owner?

days.title: Binary, hex & how data is represented
tasks: Learn binary and hexadecimal counting (CS50 week 0 notes)
Learn ASCII - every character is a number
Play with CyberChef 'To Binary', 'To Hex', 'From Hex'
days.challenge: By hand: convert 192 to binary and hex, and 0x41 to its ASCII letter. Verify in CyberChef.

days.title: What is a network? LAN vs WAN
tasks: TryHackMe: 'What Is Networking?'
Professor Messer Network+: watch the networking intro videos
days.challenge: Draw your home network (router, phone, laptop, ISP) and add the diagram to your notes.

days.title: IP addressing - public vs private
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Intro to Networking'
Learn the private ranges: 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16
days.challenge: Find your private IP and your public IP. Explain in your notes why they are different.

days.title: Subnetting & CIDR
tasks: Learn CIDR notation, network/broadcast address, usable hosts
Do 10 practice questions on subnettingpractice.com
days.challenge: For 192.168.10.0/26: network address, broadcast address, usable host count? (Check with /challenge too.)

days.title: MAC addresses, Ethernet & ARP
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Layer 2'
Learn how ARP maps IP -> MAC and why ARP spoofing works
days.challenge: Read your ARP table and look up the vendor of your router's MAC address.

days.title: Week 2 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Processes, memory & filesystems - what an OS does; Binary, hex & how data is represented; What is a network? LAN vs WAN; IP addressing - public vs private; Subnetting & CIDR; MAC addresses, Ethernet & ARP
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Processes, memory & filesystems - what an OS does' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Ports, protocols, TCP vs UDP
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Networking Concepts'
Learn TCP (reliable, connection) vs UDP (fast, connectionless)
days.challenge: From memory, list 15 well-known ports and their services (21, 22, 25, 53, 80, 443, 445, 3389 ...).

days.title: TCP handshake + your first Wireshark capture
tasks: Install Wireshark
TryHackMe: 'Network Traffic Basics'
Capture traffic while you open a website
days.challenge: In your capture, find the SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK of one TCP connection. Screenshot the 3 packets.

days.title: DNS in detail
tasks: TryHackMe: 'DNS in Detail'
Learn record types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS
days.challenge: Use `dig` to find the MX and TXT records of owasp.org. What does the SPF TXT record tell you?

days.title: DHCP, routing & NAT
tasks: Learn DHCP DORA (Discover, Offer, Request, Ack)
Learn how NAT lets many private IPs share one public IP
Professor Messer: routing & NAT videos
days.challenge: Run `traceroute google.com`. How many hops? Which hop is your own router?

days.title: HTTP & HTTPS
tasks: TryHackMe: 'HTTP in Detail'
Learn methods (GET/POST), status codes, headers
days.challenge: Run `curl -I https://owasp.org`. Write down the status code and 3 security-related headers you see.

days.title: TLS & certificates
tasks: Learn how TLS protects HTTP: certificates, CAs, handshake (high level)
Inspect a website's certificate in your browser
days.challenge: For github.com find: certificate issuer, expiry date, and which TLS version was negotiated.

days.title: Week 3 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Ports, protocols, TCP vs UDP; TCP handshake + your first Wireshark capture; DNS in detail; DHCP, routing & NAT; HTTP & HTTPS; TLS & certificates
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Ports, protocols, TCP vs UDP' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Firewalls
tasks: Learn stateless vs stateful firewalls
Configure `ufw` in your Ubuntu VM
days.challenge: Enable ufw, allow only SSH (22) inbound, then list the rules with `sudo ufw status verbose`.

days.title: The OSI model
tasks: Learn the 7 layers (Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away)
TryHackMe: 'Network Security Essentials'
days.challenge: Map these to an OSI layer: switch, router, HTTP, TCP, IP, Ethernet, TLS, DNS, MAC address, cable.

days.title: TCP/IP model + Wireshark filters
tasks: Compare TCP/IP (4 layers) with OSI (7 layers)
Practice Wireshark display filters: `ip.addr==`, `tcp.port==`, `http`, `dns`
Download `http.cap` from Wireshark Sample Captures
days.challenge: Open http.cap: what URL was requested and what web server answered?

days.title: Networking checkpoint: build a cheat sheet
tasks: Write a one-page networking cheat sheet (ports, OSI, subnetting, DNS records, commands)
Push it to your cybersec-notes repo
TryHackMe: 'Beginner Path Intro'
days.challenge: Without notes, explain what happens when you type a URL in the browser and press Enter (DNS -> TCP -> TLS -> HTTP).

days.title: Linux filesystem & navigation
tasks: Linux Journey: 'Command Line' section
Learn the hierarchy: /etc, /home, /var, /tmp, /usr, /bin
Read OverTheWire Bandit rules, then solve level 0
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 0 -> 1. Save the password in a private notes file (not on GitHub!).

days.title: Files & directories
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Linux Fundamentals Part 1'
Practice cp, mv, rm, mkdir, touch, special filenames (`-`, spaces, hidden)
days.challenge: Solve Bandit levels 1 -> 4.

days.title: Week 4 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Firewalls; The OSI model; TCP/IP model + Wireshark filters; Networking checkpoint: build a cheat sheet; Linux filesystem & navigation; Files & directories
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Firewalls' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Finding files: find & file
tasks: Learn `find` with -name, -type, -size, -user, -group
Learn `file` to detect file types
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 4 -> 7.

days.title: grep, sort, uniq & pipes
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Linux Fundamentals Part 2'
Learn pipes `|` and redirection `>`, `>>`, `2>/dev/null`
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 7 -> 10.

days.title: Encoding tricks on the command line
tasks: Learn `base64 -d`, `tr` (ROT13), `xxd`, gzip/bzip2/tar
Bandit 12 is long - be patient and use a /tmp working dir
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 10 -> 13.

days.title: Permissions, users & groups
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Linux Fundamentals Part 3'
Learn rwx, octal (755, 640), chown, sudo, /etc/passwd vs /etc/shadow
days.challenge: In your VM create user `analyst`, group `soc`, and a folder only the soc group can read (mode 750).

days.title: SSH & keys
tasks: Learn SSH key auth (private vs public key)
Generate an ed25519 key and SSH from your host into your VM
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 13 -> 15 and log into your own VM with a key instead of a password.

days.title: Networking from the terminal: nc & openssl
tasks: Learn `nc` (netcat) to talk to ports
Learn `openssl s_client` for TLS ports
Learn basic `nmap` on localhost only
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 15 -> 18.

days.title: Week 5 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Finding files: find & file; grep, sort, uniq & pipes; Encoding tricks on the command line; Permissions, users & groups; SSH & keys; Networking from the terminal: nc & openssl
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Finding files: find & file' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Processes & services
tasks: Learn ps, top, kill, jobs, systemctl, journalctl
Install nginx in your VM and manage it as a service
days.challenge: Install nginx, stop/start it, and find its log lines with `journalctl -u nginx`.

days.title: Package management, PATH & environment variables
tasks: Learn apt (install, remove, search), dpkg
Learn env vars: `$PATH`, `$HOME`, `export`, `.bashrc`
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 18 -> 21. Then add `~/bin` to your PATH permanently.

days.title: Cron & scheduled jobs
tasks: Learn crontab syntax (`m h dom mon dow`)
Understand why writable cron scripts are a privilege-escalation risk
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 21 -> 24.

days.title: Linux logs
tasks: Explore /var/log (auth.log, syslog)
TryHackMe: 'Intro to Logs'
days.challenge: Make 3 failed SSH logins to your VM, then find them in /var/log/auth.log with one grep command.

days.title: Bandit: scripting & git
tasks: Bandit 24 needs a small brute-force loop (bash)
Bandit 27-31 teach git - use `git log`, branches and tags
days.challenge: Solve Bandit 24 -> 25 and 27 -> 32. (25-26 are optional tricky ones.)

days.title: Windows fundamentals 1
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Windows Fundamentals 1'
Explore: file system (NTFS), Task Manager, services.msc
days.challenge: List 3 Windows services, their startup type and the account they run as.

days.title: Week 6 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Processes & services; Package management, PATH & environment variables; Cron & scheduled jobs; Linux logs; Bandit: scripting & git; Windows fundamentals 1
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Processes & services' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Windows users, permissions & UAC
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Windows Fundamentals 2'
Learn local users/groups, UAC, NTFS permissions
days.challenge: Run `whoami /all` and explain 3 privileges listed.

days.title: Windows command line
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Windows Command Line'
days.challenge: Use `netstat -ano` + `tasklist` to find which program owns one listening port.

days.title: Windows Event Logs
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Windows Fundamentals 3'
Open Event Viewer -> Windows Logs -> Security
days.challenge: Find a 4624 (successful logon) and 4625 (failed logon) event. What logon type did each have?

days.title: PowerShell basics
tasks: Microsoft Learn: PowerShell 101 (chapters 1-3)
Learn Get-Help, Get-Command, Get-Member, the pipeline
days.challenge: One-liner: show the 5 processes using the most CPU (`Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5`).

days.title: How web applications work
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Web Application Basics'
MDN: An overview of HTTP
Remember: no SQL injection before you understand SQL and web apps
days.challenge: Open DevTools on any site and list every request header your browser sent for the main page.

days.title: HTML & JavaScript basics
tasks: MDN: Getting started with the web (HTML + JS)
Re-read your own todolist2 `script.js` - you already wrote JS!
days.challenge: Your todo app uses `textContent`. Write in notes why `innerHTML` with user input would be dangerous (hint: XSS).

days.title: Week 7 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Windows users, permissions & UAC; Windows command line; Windows Event Logs; PowerShell basics; How web applications work; HTML & JavaScript basics
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Windows users, permissions & UAC' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Cookies, sessions, authentication vs authorization
tasks: MDN: HTTP cookies
Learn session IDs, cookie flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite
Authentication = who you are, Authorization = what you may do
days.challenge: Log into a site you use. Which cookie is the session cookie, and which flags does it have?

days.title: REST APIs & JSON
tasks: Learn REST verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), JSON, status codes
Call the public GitHub API
days.challenge: `curl https://api.github.com/users/<your-username>` and use jq to print only your public repo count.

days.title: SQL basics 1
tasks: SQLBolt lessons 1-6 (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT)
days.challenge: Finish SQLBolt lessons 1-6.

days.title: SQL basics 2
tasks: SQLBolt lessons 7-12 (JOINs, NULL, expressions, aggregates)
days.challenge: Finish SQLBolt lessons 7-12.

days.title: SQL basics 3
tasks: SQLBolt lessons 13-18 (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE)
Think: how is a login query built? `SELECT * FROM users WHERE name='?' AND pass='?'`
days.challenge: Finish SQLBolt. Then write in notes what happens to that login query if the name is `admin'--`.

days.title: Python 1: variables, types, conditionals
tasks: Install Python 3 + VS Code
CS50P Lecture 0 (Functions, Variables) and Lecture 1 (Conditionals)
days.challenge: Write `grade.py`: read a score 0-100 and print A/B/C/D/F. Handle invalid input.

days.title: Week 8 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Cookies, sessions, authentication vs authorization; REST APIs & JSON; SQL basics 1; SQL basics 2; SQL basics 3; Python 1: variables, types, conditionals
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Cookies, sessions, authentication vs authorization' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Python 2: loops & functions
tasks: CS50P Lecture 2 (Loops)
TryHackMe: 'Python Basics'
days.challenge: Write `is_prime(n)` and print all primes below 100.

days.title: Python 3: lists & dictionaries
tasks: Practice list/dict operations, comprehensions
Automate the Boring Stuff: chapters 4-5

links.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python

days.challenge: Count word frequency in any .txt file and print the top 10 words.

days.title: Python 4: files & exceptions
tasks: CS50P Lecture 3 (Exceptions) and Lecture 6 (File I/O)
days.challenge: Parse your VM's /var/log/auth.log and count failed SSH logins per IP address.

days.title: Python 5: modules & command-line arguments
tasks: Learn `import`, `argparse`, `sys.argv`, virtual environments (`python -m venv`)
days.challenge: Turn yesterday's log parser into `logparse.py --file auth.log --top 5`.

days.title: Python 6: HTTP requests
tasks: Automate the Boring Stuff: Web Scraping chapter
Install `requests` in a venv

links.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python

days.challenge: Script: given a URL, print status code and whether HSTS, CSP and X-Frame-Options headers are present.

days.title: Python 7: sockets & a banner grabber
tasks: Learn the `socket` module: connect, send, recv
TryHackMe: 'Custom Tooling with Python'
days.challenge: Grab the SSH banner of YOUR VM with a 10-line Python script.

days.title: Week 9 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Python 2: loops & functions; Python 3: lists & dictionaries; Python 4: files & exceptions; Python 5: modules & command-line arguments; Python 6: HTTP requests; Python 7: sockets & a banner grabber
Redo the hardest exercise of the week without looking at your notes
Write a 'What I learned / What confused me' note and push it to cybersec-notes
Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Python 2: loops & functions' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

days.title: Python 8: build a port scanner (your own VM only)
tasks: Combine sockets + threads (`concurrent.futures`)
Only scan machines you own - roadmap rule #1
days.challenge: Scan ports 1-1024 on your VM in under 10 seconds. Compare with `nmap` output.

days.title: Python 9: hashing & a password strength checker
tasks: Learn `hashlib` (md5, sha256) and why fast hashes are bad for passwords (use bcrypt/argon2)
days.challenge: Build `pwcheck.py`: score length, character classes, and reject passwords from a small common-password list.

days.title: Bash scripting 1
tasks: learnshell.org: basics, variables, arrays, loops, conditions
days.challenge: Write `sweep.sh` that pings 192.168.x.1-254 on YOUR home network and prints live hosts.

days.title: Bash scripting 2: functions & automation
tasks: Learn functions, `$1 $2 $@`, exit codes, `set -euo pipefail`
days.challenge: Write `backup.sh` that tars your notes folder with a date in the filename; schedule it with cron.

days.title: PowerShell scripting
tasks: Microsoft Learn: PowerShell 101 chapters 4-6 (functions, scripts)
days.challenge: Script that lists local users, whether they are enabled, and their last logon (`Get-LocalUser`).

days.title: (Optional) C basics: memory, pointers, stack
tasks: CS50x Week 4: Memory - pointers, malloc, stack vs heap
Optional for web/SOC paths, important for RE & pwn later
days.challenge: Write a C program that prints the address of a local variable and a malloc'd buffer. Which is stack, which is heap?

days.title: Week 10 review & write-up day
tasks: Re-read your notes for this week: Python 8: build a port scanner (your own VM only); Python 9: hashing & a password strength checker; Bash scripting 1; Bash scripting 2: functions & automation; PowerShell scripting; (Optional) C basics: memory, pointers, stack

Solve 2 bonus challenges (/challenge in the bot or on the dashboard)
days.challenge: Teach-back: explain 'Python 8: build a port scanner (your own VM only)' out loud in 2 minutes as if to a friend.

Write a README for each: problem, usage, what you learned
days.challenge: Push the repo and pin it on your GitHub profile.

days.title: CIA triad & AAA
tasks: Professor Messer Security+: security concepts videos
Learn Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability + Authentication, Authorization, Accounting
days.challenge: For each: ransomware, a leaked database, a tampered bank transaction - which CIA pillar is hit?

Learn salting + slow hashing (bcrypt, argon2)
Enable MFA on your email and GitHub today
days.challenge: Explain in notes why SMS is the weakest second factor and why salts stop rainbow tables.

days.title: Encoding vs hashing vs encryption
tasks: TryHackMe: 'CyberChef: The Basics'
Encoding = reversible, no key. Hashing = one-way. Encryption = reversible with key
days.challenge: In CyberChef: Base64 'hello', MD5 'hello', AES-encrypt 'hello'. Explain which one is NOT security.

days.title: Symmetric vs asymmetric cryptography
tasks: Learn AES (shared key) vs RSA/ECC (key pairs), key exchange
Use openssl on the command line
days.challenge: AES-encrypt a file with a password, then generate an RSA key pair and encrypt a short message with the public key.

days.title: Hashes & password cracking concepts
tasks: TryHackMe: 'Crack the Hash'
Learn hash identification and wordlists (rockyou)
days.challenge: Finish Level 1 of Crack the Hash.

days.title: Week 11 review & write-up day
